paragraphs: K16 Solutions sells data software to colleges and universities, prying campus information out of the systems that hold it and handing it back in usable shape. Everything runs on one patented platform called Scaffold, spanning data warehousing, live LMS course backup, and student data archiving. A fourth product moves online course content from one learning management system to another.

The warehouse product connects to a campus LMS, SIS, CRM, and ERP through public and private APIs. Data lands in a structure specific to higher education, so a student, a course, and an enrollment get defined once instead of differently in every report. The copy lives in the institution's own governed environment, built on Snowflake and hosted on AWS. Staff can ask in plain language, and the SQL the system writes is shown rather than hidden.

Campus customers named on the site include San Diego State University. The company reports more than 12 million courses archived, and says its founders worked together for over 18 years across multiple higher education institutions. For institutions facing audits, it lists ISO 27001 certification by Schellman, SOC 2 Type II, data masking, and FERPA-aligned handling of student records.

quote.text: Higher ed IT leaders run the systems and control the data layer underneath them.
